nodes.name: One-step dual-confinement pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: Ptₙ - Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC was prepared using a "one-step dual-confinement pyrolysis" strategy (Figure 1a). The so-called dual confinement here refers to the fact that Pt₁ is confined by both four-fold hollow (O4H) site of confined PMo₁₂ and N-pointed cavity in NPC through Pt-O and Pt-N, respectively (viz. Pt₁-Pt_{1@PMo₁₂}/NPC). Then, both Ptₙ - Pt₁/NPC and Ptₙ - Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC were obtained through pyrolyzing Pt₁/NPC and Pt₁ - Pt_{1@PMo12}/NPC, respectively.
nodes.source_text: Ptₙ - Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC was prepared using a "one-step dual-confinement pyrolysis" strategy (Figure 1a)... Then, both Ptₙ - Pt₁/NPC and Ptₙ - Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC were obtained through pyrolyzing Pt₁/NPC and Pt₁ - Pt_{1@PMo12}/NPC, respectively.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: The HER performance was examined in a three-electrode system in 1.0 M KOH and all potentials were referenced to a reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) with 90% iR correction (Figure S38, Supporting Information). As shown by linear scanning voltammetry (LSV) curves in Figure 3a, Pt_n - Pt_{1@Mo2C} / NPC exhibits a low overpotential of 24 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2} (η_{10}), which is significantly better than 20% Pt/C, Pt_n-Pt_1/NPC and Mo_2C/NPC. At 100 mA cm^{-2} Pt_n - Pt_{1@Mo2C} / NPC demonstrates an overpotential of 84 mV ... Pt_n - Pt_{1@Mo2C} / NPC shows a lower Tafel slope (30.9 mV dec^{-1}) ... ultrahigh mass activity (4.33 mA μg Pt^{-1} at an overpotential of 100 mV) ≈ 8.8 times higher than commercial Pt/C ... j_ECSA value (0.121 mA cm^{-2}) ... Upon 10 000 cyclic voltammogram (CV) cycles ... minimal performance drop ... under 10 mA cm^{-2}, Pt_n - Pt_{1@Mo2C} / NPC exhibits no significant attenuation after 100 h

nodes.characterization_summary: No nanoparticles observed in Pt_1/NPC and Pt_1-Pt_{1@PMo12}/NPC precursors.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Exactly, nanoparticles are not observed in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figures S7 and S8, Supporting Information).

properties.description: nanoparticles or clusters labeled in red circles

properties.features: dark background with bright circular spots (nanoparticles)

nodes.characterization_summary: No obvious diffraction peaks of Pt nanoparticles or PMo12, indicating atomic dispersion on NPC surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns show no obvious diffraction peaks of Pt nanoparticles or PMo12, indicating that Pt and PMo12 species may atomically disperse on the surface of NPC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt_1/NPC shows uniformly dispersed Pt atoms; Pt_1-Pt_{1@PMo12}/NPC shows individual Pt atoms and Mo clusters ~1 nm with embedded Pt_1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM images elucidate that unlike Pt_1/NPC (Figure 1b; Figure S11, Supporting Information) with only uniformly dispersed Pt atoms, Pt_1-Pt_{1@PMo12}/NPC shows individual Pt atoms and Mo clusters of ~1 nm, with bright Pt_1 embedded.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge absorption threshold between Pt foil and PtO2 for both precursors, confirming atomic Pt states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) of Pt L3-edge shows that both the absorption threshold of Pt_1/NPC and Pt_1-Pt_{1@PMo12}/NPC is between that of Pt foil and PtO2, re-corroborating that Pt species in both systems are in atomic states.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt_1/NPC: Pt-N (CN* ~4) at ≈2.25Å; Pt_1-Pt_{1@PMo12}/NPC: Pt-N (CN* ~4) at 2.26Å and Pt-O (CN* ~4) at 1.98Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt_1/NPC shows only Pt-N bond (coordination number, CN*, ~4) at ≈2.25Å. Differently, Pt_1-Pt_{1@PMo12}/NPC displays both Pt-N (CN*, ~4) and Pt-O (CN*, ~4) with broader peak shapes at 2.26 and 1.98 Å, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt_n - Pt_1/NPC: Pt_n ~5 nm with (111) faces, irregular shapes, Pt_1 co-loaded near Pt_n.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Pt_n - Pt_1/NPC, Pt_n of ~5 nm in diameter with exposed (111) crystal faces are observed... HAADF-STEM images exhibit that all Pt_n display irregular shapes and Pt_1 (red circle) are co-loaded near the Pt_n.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt_n - Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC: Pt_n ~3 nm uniform size, alternating light-dark pattern due to Mo2C, Pt_n surrounded by ultrafine Mo2C with confined Pt_1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to Pt_n - Pt_1/NPC, nanoparticles in Pt_n - Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC show increased uniformity with a smaller size of ~3 nm... Figure 2e reveals that the Pt_n (marked by red circles) are uniformly surrounded by ultrafine Mo2C, with brightly visible Pt_1 confined.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice spacings of 0.229 nm and 0.26 nm correspond to (101) and (100) planes of Mo2C; brighter spots confirm atomically dispersed Pt in Mo2C lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Lattice spacings of 0.229 and 0.26 nm are measured, which can be distinguished as (101) and (100) crystal planes of Mo2C. Brighter spots in the FFT pattern and elevated intensity of isolated sites in line intensity profiles further reveal the atomically dispersed Pt in the lattice of Mo2C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Presence of Pt_n and β-Mo2C crystalline phases in Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC; distinct α-Mo2C peak after Pt loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD pattern also confirms the presence of both Pt_n and β-Mo2C crystalline phases in Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC. Compared to Mo2C/NPC, Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC exhibits a distinct characteristic peak of metastable α-Mo2C after Pt loading.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt_n-Pt1/NPC: Pt0 at 71.44/74.64 eV, Ptδ+ at 72.6/75.8 eV; Pt_n-Pt1@Mo2C/NPC: Pt0 at 71.6/74.66 eV, Ptδ+ at 72.86/75.9 eV (higher proportion); positive shift suggests electron transfer from Pt1 to Mo2C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Pt 4f spectra show two pairs of peaks corresponding to Pt0 at 71.44 and 74.64 eV (71.6 and 74.66 eV), and Ptδ+ at 72.6 and 75.8 eV (72.86 and 75.9 eV) for Pt_n-Pt1/NPC and Pt_n-Pt1@Mo2C/NPC, respectively. The higher proportion Ptδ+ peak in Pt_n-Pt1@Mo2C/NPC implies more Pt1 are anchored on Mo2C... Pt 4f XPS spectra of Pt_n-Pt1@Mo2C/NPC exhibit a positive shift compared with Pt_n-Pt1/NPC, suggesting possible electron transfer from Pt1 to Mo2C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge absorption threshold of Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC between Pt foil and PtO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt L3-edge XANES shows the absorption threshold of Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC between Pt foil and PtO2 consistent with XPS findings.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC: Pt-Pt bonds from Pt_n, Pt-Mo (2.77Å, CN*≈1), dominant Pt-C (2.02Å, CN*≈3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: EXAFS fitting results show a dominant Pt-C bond (2.02Å, CN*≈3) and a Pt-Mo bond (2.77Å, CN*≈1), again suggesting that Pt_1 anchor on Mo2C by replacing Mo atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Reduced specific surface area for Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC due to presence of Mo2C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The alternating light-dark pattern is likely due to the presence of Mo2C (yellow circle), as Mo has a lower atomic number than Pt, which also induces reduced specific surface area of Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC (Figure S22 and Table S3, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo2C/NPC vs Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC shows higher proportion of low valence Mo2+ and Mo4+, indicating Pt1 stabilizes Mo2C surface against oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with Mo2C/NPC, Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC shows a higher proportion of low valence Mo2+ and Mo4+, hinting that the presence of Pt1 may stabilize Mo2C surface against oxidation.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings affirm atomically dispersed Pt in Mo2C lattice of Pt_n-Pt_{1@Mo2C}/NPC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mappings also affirm this (Figure S25, Supporting Information).
